cli.usage:
brain-kit {version}

Usage: brain-kit <command> [options]

Commands available in this version:
  init [dir] [--lang en|pt-BR] [--yes] [--from-answers <file>]           create a new vault in an empty or new directory, asking one question at a time
  init --adopt [dir] [--lang en|pt-BR] [--yes] [--from-answers <file>]   bring an existing vault under the kit, writing only its configuration and manifest
  update [dir] [--check | --accept <path>]                               refresh the files the kit manages, never overwriting one you edited
  hook <stop|session-start>                                              entry point for the Claude Code plugin hooks (reads the event JSON from stdin)
  validate [dir] [--only-problems] [--json]                              check a vault against the Open Knowledge Format and this vault's own house rules
  lint [dir] [--rule <id>...] [--base auto|worktree|merge-base|all] [--json]   check a vault's own health rules (orphans, tables, secrets, and more)
  doctor [dir] [--json] [--only <id,...>]                                check that this machine and this vault are ready for the kit (tools, gate, configuration, state directory)
  --version                                                              print the version
  --help                                                                 print this help

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failure, 2 usage or not inside a vault, 3 degraded, 4 required source not read, 69 network or connector unavailable, 75 postponed (retry later).
validate.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit validate: "{dir}" is not a directory.
validate.no_vault: brain-kit validate: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and {index}).
validate.explain_must: These findings mean the bundle is not conformant to the Open Knowledge Format.
validate.explain_should: These findings mean the vault departs from the format's own guidance, without breaking conformance.
validate.explain_house: These findings mean the vault departs from its own house rules: what its configuration declares, plus the defaults it left in place. The format defines no conformance tier for them.
validate.explain_defect: These findings carry a ruler and level this command does not recognize. This is a defect in brain-kit itself, not in your vault; please report it.
validate.explain_stale: This is informational only and never affects the exit code.
validate.stale_none: No note has passed its stale_after date.
validate.verdict_clean: Result: no findings. The vault is conformant and has no departures.
validate.verdict_clean_with_stale: Result: no conformance or house findings. The vault is conformant; the stale notes listed above are informational only and do not change this.
validate.verdict_warnings_only: Result: the vault is conformant. Every finding above was downgraded to a warning; nothing blocks this run.
validate.verdict_not_blocking: Result: the findings above do not fail this run, because this vault sets validate.fail_on to "{failOn}". Set it to "any" to fail on all of them.
validate.verdict_blocking: Result: the vault is conformant to the format, but findings above (guidance or house rules) block this run.
validate.verdict_broken: Result: the vault is not conformant to the format.
validate.verdict_unexpected: Result: at least one finding could not be classified; this run cannot say whether the vault is conformant. See the tool defect section above.
common.shape_unreadable: {field} is present but its shape could not be read (see PARSER_LIMITS in src/frontmatter.mjs)
common.timestamp_form: {field} "{value}" is not an ISO 8601 datetime with an explicit UTC offset, which section 5 requires for every timestamp-valued key
spec.type_required.unterminated: frontmatter opens with "---" but is never closed with a second one, so type cannot be confirmed; close the block
spec.type_required.no_frontmatter: type is required but missing (the file has no frontmatter at all)
spec.type_required.no_type_key: type is required but missing (this file has frontmatter, but no type key in it)
spec.type_required.empty: type is present but empty; it must be a non-empty string
spec.index_no_frontmatter.outside_root: index.md is reserved and must carry no frontmatter (only the root index may declare okf_version)
spec.index_no_frontmatter.extra_key: the root index may declare only okf_version and nothing else; found "{found}"
spec.log_format.has_frontmatter: log.md is reserved and should carry no frontmatter
spec.log_format.heading_calendar: log heading "## {heading}" is in YYYY-MM-DD form but names a day that does not exist; section 9 requires a real ISO 8601 date
spec.log_format.heading_form: log heading "## {heading}" is a date written in another form; section 9 requires date headings in ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD form
spec.log_format.heading_not_a_date: log heading "## {heading}" is not a date heading; a log groups its entries under dates
spec.log_format.ordering: log dates must run from most recent to oldest; "{date}" comes after "{previous}"
spec.generated_actor.missing_actor: generated.by is required but missing or empty
spec.verified_events.empty: verified is present but carries no events; remove the key or add at least one with by and at
spec.verified_events.missing_actor: verified[{index}].by is required but missing or empty
spec.verified_events.missing_timestamp: verified[{index}].at is required but missing or empty
spec.status_enum.invalid: status "{value}" is not one of draft, stable, deprecated
spec.stale_after_format.invalid: stale_after "{value}" must be an ISO 8601 datetime with an explicit UTC offset; section 5 requires this for every timestamp-valued key, so a plain date is no longer accepted here
spec.sources_resource.missing_resource: sources[{index}] is missing a non-empty resource
house.required_fields.missing: {key} is required by this vault's own configuration but is missing
house.required_fields.empty: {key} is required by this vault's own configuration but is empty
house.forbidden_fields.present: {key} is forbidden by this vault's own configuration but is present
house.type_enum.invalid: type "{value}" is not one of this vault's allowed types: {allowed}
house.extension_fields.boolean: {field} "{value}" must be a boolean (true or false)
house.extension_fields.date: {field} "{value}" must be an ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD)
house.extension_fields.enum: {field} "{value}" is not one of this vault's allowed values: {allowed}
house.link_style.file_relative: link {seen} starts with a slash, which resolves against the host, not the repository, and breaks where a human reviews the change; this vault requires file-relative links
house.link_style.bundle_absolute: link {seen} does not start with a slash; this vault requires bundle-absolute links
house.link_target_exists.broken: link target "{target}" does not resolve to anything in this vault (resolved to "{resolved}")
house.link_target_exists.unwalked: link target "{target}" exists on disk but is not part of what this command walked (resolved to "{resolved}"); it sits under validate.ignore_paths, a dot-entry or node_modules, so this run cannot vouch for it
house.no_wikilinks.forbidden: [[{target}]] is a wikilink, which this vault forbids; use a standard markdown link instead
house.root_okf_version.missing: the root index does not declare okf_version, which this vault requires
house.root_okf_version.mismatch: the root index declares okf_version "{value}" but this vault is configured for "{expected}"
lint.index_completeness.missing_index: the directory "{dir}" holds a markdown file but has no index.md
lint.index_completeness.dir_not_linked: the root index does not link the first-level directory "{dir}"
lint.orphans.unreachable: this note is not reachable by following links from the root index
lint.columns.missing_table: this file has no table to check against its configured column headings
lint.tables.missing_blank_line: this table has no blank line before its header row; this change touched the table, so the whole table was checked, not just the lines it added
lint.tables.missing_blank_line_full: this table has no blank line before its header row; this run checked the whole vault, so every table was checked, whether or not anything changed
lint.tables.duplicate_row: this data row duplicates the row at line {line}; this change touched the table, so the whole table was checked, not just the lines it added
lint.tables.duplicate_row_full: this data row duplicates the row at line {line}; this run checked the whole vault, so every table was checked, whether or not anything changed
lint.tables.cell_too_long: cell {index} has {length} characters, over the configured maximum of {max}; this change touched the table, so the whole table was checked, not just the lines it added
lint.tables.cell_too_long_full: cell {index} has {length} characters, over the configured maximum of {max}; this run checked the whole vault, so every table was checked, whether or not anything changed
lint.style.forbidden_char: this line was added by this change and uses the forbidden character "{char}"; style only judges lines a change added, not prose that was already in the vault
lint.style.forbidden_char_full: this line uses the forbidden character "{char}"; this run checked the whole vault, so every line was judged, not only lines a change added
lint.style.nothing_configured: the style rule is switched on for this vault but lint.style.forbidden_chars names no character, so this rule had nothing at all to look for; give it characters to forbid, or set lint.style to "off"
lint.secrets.pattern_matched_full: a line matches a secret-shaped pattern ({pattern}); never paste, print or share the matched text, rotate the credential now and follow the incident response steps in SECURITY.md
lint.secrets.truncated: this file carries more secret-shaped matches than could be listed: {shown} shown out of {total} found; treat every one as leaked, not only the ones named above, and follow SECURITY.md
lint.secrets.file_too_large: this file is {bytes} bytes, over the {max} byte limit for one file, so it was NOT scanned for secrets, and this run fails rather than calling it clean: nothing here was checked, which is not the same as nothing being here; if the file is known to be safe, list it under lint.secrets.exclude_paths, where the exclusion shows in review
lint.secrets.pattern_is_a_credential: an entry in privacy.secret_patterns is itself shaped like a real credential; that list is for DETECTION patterns, never for the secret you want detected, so rotate that credential now, remove it from the configuration and follow SECURITY.md
lint.privacy.linked_into_confidential: this file sits outside every confidential directory but links into one ("{target}"), exposing a confidential note from a place meant to be shared more broadly
lint.privacy.confidential_outside: this note carries {field}: true but sits outside every directory the configuration marks confidential
lint.attribution.missing_source_id: sources[{index}] has no id, so no footnote can ever anchor a claim to it
lint.attribution.unknown_footnote: this footnote key ("{key}") matches no id declared in sources; a footnote is meant to anchor a claim to one of the ids listed there
lint.attribution.source_not_anchored: sources declares the id "{id}" but no footnote in the body ever cites it; when a note draws on more than one source, this check expects each one to be anchored somewhere in the body
lint.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit lint: "{dir}" is not a directory.
lint.no_vault: brain-kit lint: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and {index}).
lint.unknown_base: brain-kit lint: unknown base "{base}" (expected one of: {ids}).
lint.unknown_rule: brain-kit lint: unknown rule "{rule}" (expected one of: {ids}).
lint.explain_error: These findings are treated as errors: this run fails because of them.
lint.explain_warn: These findings are warnings: they never fail this run.
lint.verdict_clean_but_partial: Result: no findings, but this run did not check everything (see the scope line above, and the skipped count below, if any); a clean report from a partial run is not the same as a clean vault.
lint.verdict_warnings_only: Result: only warnings above; this run does not fail because of them.
lint.verdict_failing: Result: this run fails because of the error(s) above.
lint.verdict_failing_too_large: Result: this run fails because of the error(s) above, {count} of them a file too large to scan for secrets, which was not read at all; that is not the same as clean.
lint.verdict_degraded: Result: this run is degraded ({causes}), so its results are incomplete; treat the findings above as partial, fix the cause named for each one, and rerun.
lint.degraded_part.timed_out: {count} file(s) took too long to scan for secrets and timed out
lint.degraded_part.scan_failed: {count} file(s) could not be scanned for secrets
lint.degraded_part.listing_failed: git could not list the files this vault would publish
lint.explain_defect: These are not findings about your vault: this tool itself failed to finish checking it. Every finding above them from a rule that did complete is still real; nothing above is.
lint.tool_defect.rule_crashed: the "{rule}" rule crashed and produced no results at all: {message}
lint.tool_defect.file_scan_failed: the secrets scan on this file failed and was abandoned rather than reported as complete: {message}
lint.tool_defect.file_scan_timed_out: the secrets scan on this file ran out of time and was abandoned rather than reported as complete: {message}
lint.tool_defect.file_read_failed: this file could not be read at all (error {code}), so it was not scanned for secrets
lint.tool_defect.file_name_undecodable: this file's name is not valid UTF-8, so it cannot be opened by name here and was not scanned for secrets; rename it
lint.tool_defect.publishable_list_failed: git could not list the files this vault would publish (git exited {status}), so the secrets rule read nothing at all; fix the repository and rerun
lint.scope.outside_repo: Scope: not inside a git repository, so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.scope.all_explicit: Scope: "all" was requested, so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.scope.no_commits: Scope: this repository has no commit yet, so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.scope.worktree_explicit: Scope: "worktree" was requested, checking what differs from HEAD.
lint.scope.merge_base_explicit: Scope: "merge-base" was requested, checking what changed since the merge base with "{defaultBranch}".
lint.scope.merge_base_unavailable: Scope: "merge-base" was requested, but no usable default branch or common ancestor was found, so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.scope.merge_base_same_as_current: Scope: "merge-base" was requested, but the default branch is the branch already checked out, so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.scope.auto_since_merge_base: Scope: "auto", checking everything committed since the merge base with "{defaultBranch}", plus the current worktree and any untracked file.
lint.scope.auto_merge_base_unavailable: Scope: "auto", but no usable merge base was found, checking what differs from HEAD, plus any untracked file.
lint.scope.auto_no_default_branch: Scope: "auto", but no default branch could be identified, checking what differs from HEAD, plus any untracked file.
lint.scope.auto_on_default_branch: Scope: "auto", already on the default branch, checking what differs from HEAD, plus any untracked file.
lint.scope.auto_on_default_branch_clean: Scope: "auto", already on the default branch with nothing left to compare against (a clean tree, nothing untracked), so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.secrets_reach_git: The secrets rule is never narrowed by the scope above: it read {count} file(s), every one git tracks or would add here, dot-files included, each as it stands in the working tree; files git ignores were not read, and neither is anything only a commit holds.
lint.secrets_reach_walk: The secrets rule is never narrowed by the scope above: this is not a git repository, so it read {count} file(s), every one the vault walk includes plus dot-files, except .git and anything under node_modules.
lint.scope_ignored_paths: Not checked at all, by this vault's own choice: validate.ignore_paths excludes {paths}, so nothing under those prefixes was read by any rule that ran.
lint.scope_ignored_paths_secrets_still_r: Not checked by the note rules, by this vault's own choice: validate.ignore_paths excludes {paths} from every rule but secrets, which still read every file git tracks or would add under them.
lint.secrets_excluded: Not scanned for secrets, by this vault's own choice: lint.secrets.exclude_paths excludes {paths}, {count} file(s) in all, and nothing under them was read by the secrets rule.
lint.secrets_exclude_unmatched: lint.secrets.exclude_paths names {paths}, which match no file this vault would publish, so they exclude nothing and those files were read: a path there is written relative to the vault root, the way git lists it, with no leading ./ or /.
lint.secrets_other_repositories: Not scanned for secrets: {paths}, each a submodule or a repository of its own, whose content is not in this repository.
lint.secrets_absent: Not scanned for secrets: {count} file(s) git tracks are missing from the working tree ({paths}), so what a commit holds for them was not read.
push_gate.usage: Usage: brain-kit push-gate <remote-name> <remote-url> --patterns personal|config (the pre-push reference lines on standard input)
push_gate.missing_remote: brain-kit push-gate: the remote name and the remote URL are required, in that order, as git hands them to a pre-push hook; refusing rather than guessing which remote this push goes to.
push_gate.missing_patterns: brain-kit push-gate: --patterns is required, naming the pattern list that judges this push ({expected}); there is no default, because a default is a list nobody chose.
push_gate.unknown_patterns: brain-kit push-gate: --patterns "{value}" is not a pattern list this gate knows (expected: {expected}); refusing rather than scanning with a list nobody chose.
push_gate.git_unrunnable: brain-kit push-gate: git could not be run ({reason}), so this gate cannot ask what the push contains; refusing to push.
push_gate.not_a_repository: brain-kit push-gate: the current directory is not inside a git repository, so there is no push here to enumerate; refusing rather than reading that as a push with nothing in it.
push_gate.enumeration_unrunnable: brain-kit push-gate: could not run the push enumeration, src/push/records.sh ({reason}); refusing to push without knowing what it carries.
push_gate.stream_too_large: brain-kit push-gate: the push enumeration listed more than {limit} bytes of records, more than this gate reads for one push; refusing rather than scanning part of it.
push_gate.enumeration_failed: brain-kit push-gate: the push enumeration exited {status}, so its list of what this push carries is not the whole push; refusing without scanning a partial list.
push_gate.enumeration_killed: brain-kit push-gate: the push enumeration was stopped by signal {signal} before it finished, so its list of what this push carries is not the whole push; refusing without scanning a partial list.
push_gate.git_killed: brain-kit push-gate: git was stopped by signal {signal} while this gate asked whether this is a repository, so it cannot say what the push contains; refusing to push.
push_gate.messages_too_large: brain-kit push-gate: the push enumeration wrote more than {limit} bytes of messages, more than this gate reads for one push; refusing without scanning.
push_gate.reference_count_mismatch: brain-kit push-gate: git sent {sent} reference line(s) for this push and the push enumeration listed {listed} reference(s), so some of what this push carries would go unscanned; refusing instead of calling it clean.
push_gate.reference_numbering: brain-kit push-gate: the push enumeration did not number its references 1 to {sent}, in the order git sent them, so its list does not describe this push; refusing instead of calling it clean.
push_gate.reference_name_mismatch: brain-kit push-gate: the destination name the push enumeration listed for reference #{number} of this push is not the one git sent on that line, so its list does not describe this push; refusing instead of calling it clean (neither name is printed).
push_gate.stdin_unreadable: brain-kit push-gate: the reference lines on standard input could not be read to the end ({reason}), so what did arrive is not the whole push; refusing instead of scanning part of it.
push_gate.not_a_vault: brain-kit push-gate: --patterns config reads this vault's {file}, and no vault was found from the current directory; refusing rather than scanning without the vault's patterns.
push_gate.config_unloadable: brain-kit push-gate: the working tree's {file} could not be loaded ({reason}), so this vault's patterns are unknown; refusing to push.
push_gate.config_outside_repository: brain-kit push-gate: this vault's {file} is outside the repository being pushed, so no default branch of it can hold one; this push is scanned with privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's copy alone.
push_gate.config_patterns_union: brain-kit push-gate: this push is scanned with the generic credential shapes and privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's {file}, from the configuration at {tips} pushed tip(s) and {carried} earlier commit(s) of this push, and from the default branch as this repository knows it ({branches}).
push_gate.default_branch_unresolved_name: brain-kit push-gate: no default branch of remote '{remote}' is known to this repository (none of its HEAD, main or master under refs/remotes/ resolves), so this push is scanned with privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's {file} and from the configurations this push carries alone. To add the default branch's, run: {command}
push_gate.default_branch_unresolved_by_u: brain-kit push-gate: '{remote}' is not the name of a remote, and no configured remote ({remotes}) has a default branch this repository knows (refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD, main or master), so this push is scanned with privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's {file} and from the configurations this push carries alone. To add them, run: git fetch --all
push_gate.default_branch_unresolved_no_r: brain-kit push-gate: '{remote}' is not the name of a remote and this repository has no remote configured, so no default branch is known and this push is scanned with privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's {file} and from the configurations this push carries alone. To add one, run: {command}
push_gate.default_branch_no_config: brain-kit push-gate: {branch}, a default branch as this repository knows it, has no {path}; it adds no patterns to this push.
push_gate.default_config_unusable: brain-kit push-gate: the {path} on {branch}, a default branch as this repository knows it, could not be used ({reason}); it adds no patterns to this push, which is scanned with the other sources.
push_gate.tip_config_unusable: brain-kit push-gate: the {path} at reference #{number} of this push could not be used ({reason}); it adds no patterns to this push, which is scanned with the other sources.
push_gate.default_branch_read_failed: brain-kit push-gate: could not read the {path} on {branch}, a default branch as this repository knows it ({reason}); refusing rather than scanning without the patterns a person merged there.
push_gate.tip_config_read_failed: brain-kit push-gate: could not read the {path} at reference #{number} of this push ({reason}); refusing rather than scanning without its patterns.
push_gate.pattern_uncompilable_working: brain-kit push-gate: a pattern in the working tree's {file} does not compile ({reason}); fix it there. Refusing to push.
push_gate.pattern_uncompilable_tip: brain-kit push-gate: a pattern in the {path} at reference #{number} of this push does not compile ({reason}); fix it in that commit. Refusing to push.
push_gate.pattern_uncompilable_default: brain-kit push-gate: a pattern in the {path} on {branch}, the default branch as this repository knows it, does not compile ({reason}). Every push is refused until it is fixed there, and a push that fixes it is refused too, so fix it through the host's own interface, then fetch. Refusing to push.
push_gate.default_branch_unresolved_unfe: brain-kit push-gate: this repository holds no remote-tracking branch of remote '{remote}', so this push is scanned with privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's {file} and from the configurations this push carries alone. If nothing is published there yet, there is no merged configuration to add and nothing to run; if this clone has simply never fetched it, run: {command}
push_gate.carried_config_list_failed: brain-kit push-gate: could not list the commits of this push that change {path} ({reason}); refusing rather than scanning without their patterns.
push_gate.carried_config_read_failed: brain-kit push-gate: could not read the {path} at commit {commit} of this push ({reason}); refusing rather than scanning without its patterns.
push_gate.carried_config_unusable: brain-kit push-gate: the {path} at commit {commit} of this push could not be used ({reason}); it adds no patterns to this push, which is scanned with the other sources.
push_gate.pattern_uncompilable_carried: brain-kit push-gate: a pattern in the {path} at commit {commit} of this push does not compile ({reason}); fix it in that commit. Refusing to push.
init.usage:
Usage: brain-kit init [dir] [--adopt] [--lang en|pt-BR] [--yes] [--from-answers <file>]

Makes dir (default: the current directory) a new vault: the language skeleton, brain-kit.config.json, .gitignore, the pre-push hook, .brain-kit/manifest.json and a git repository, plus machine.json in the state directory, outside the vault. It refuses, writing nothing, a directory that is not empty, is already a repository, or is or sits inside a vault. It never makes a commit unless the answers file says "commit": true.

With --adopt, dir is an existing vault (it has a root index.md and no brain-kit.config.json): init infers the configuration from its notes, prints every inference, and writes only brain-kit.config.json and .brain-kit/manifest.json into it, plus machine.json outside it. It never changes a note, never writes the hook, never changes the repository and never commits.

  --adopt                bring an existing vault under the kit
  --lang <code>          the vault's language
  --yes                  take the default for every answer not given, and list them
  --from-answers <file>  a JSON object with lang, name, handle, title, repo (null for not yet), private (true), timezone, and optionally email and commit

Without a terminal on stdin, every answer must come from --yes or --from-answers: init never waits for input it cannot get.
init.unknown_lang: brain-kit init: "{lang}" is not a supported language (supported: {langs}).
init.answers_unreadable: brain-kit init: cannot read the answers file {file}: {detail}
init.answers_not_json: brain-kit init: the answers file {file} is not JSON: {detail}
init.answers_not_object: brain-kit init: the answers file {file} must hold a JSON object of answers.
init.answers_unknown_key: brain-kit init: the answers file {file} has an unknown key "{key}" (known: {keys}). Nothing was written.
init.invalid_answer: brain-kit init: the answer for "{answer}" is {value}, and it must be {expected}. Nothing was written.
init.expect_handle: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or a digit
init.expect_repo: owner/name on GitHub, or null for not yet
init.expect_timezone: an IANA time zone such as Europe/Lisbon or UTC
init.private_required: brain-kit init: the vault's repository must be private. people/ and the other personal directories hold data about third parties, and a public repository would publish it. Nothing was written.
init.lang_conflict: brain-kit init: --lang says {flag} but the answers file says {file}. Nothing was written.
init.not_a_directory: brain-kit init: {dir} is not a directory. Nothing was written.
init.inside_vault: brain-kit init: {dir} is inside the brain-kit vault {vault}; a vault inside another is read by the outer one as its own notes. Nothing was written.
init.already_vault: brain-kit init: {dir} is already a brain-kit vault. To bring an existing vault up to date, use brain-kit update. Nothing was written.
init.already_repository: brain-kit init: {dir} is already a git repository. init only creates a new vault in an empty directory. If it is a vault you already keep, run brain-kit init --adopt on it instead. Nothing was written.
init.not_empty: brain-kit init: {dir} is not empty ({count} entries). init only creates a new vault in an empty or new directory, so nothing of yours is ever overwritten. If it is a vault you already keep, run brain-kit init --adopt on it instead. Nothing was written.
init.state_inside_vault: brain-kit init: the state directory {state} is inside the vault {dir}; it holds this machine's files and logs, which must never be versioned. Set BRAIN_KIT_STATE_DIR outside the vault. Nothing was written.
init.machine_exists: brain-kit init: {file} already exists, and init never overwrites it. Move it away if it belongs to a vault that no longer exists. Nothing was written.
init.git_unavailable: brain-kit init: git is not available ({detail}). Install git and run init again. Nothing was written.
init.answers_missing: brain-kit init: the answers file {file} has no "{answer}", and stdin is not a terminal to ask. Add it, or pass --yes to take the default. Nothing was written.
init.missing_answer: brain-kit init: no answer for "{answer}", and stdin is not a terminal to ask. Pass --yes to take every default, or --from-answers <file>. Nothing was written.
init.stdin_ended: brain-kit init: input ended before "{answer}" was answered. Nothing was written.
init.config_invalid: brain-kit init: the configuration built from these answers is not valid, which is a defect in brain-kit: {errors}. Nothing was written.
init.machine_invalid: brain-kit init: the machine file built for this vault is not valid, which is a defect in brain-kit: {errors}. Nothing was written.
init.using_defaults: --yes: using every default for the answers not given:
init.created: Created the vault in {dir} ({count} files recorded in .brain-kit/manifest.json).
init.state_written: Wrote this machine's settings to {file}, outside the vault.
init.commit_message: Start the vault with brain-kit init
init.committed: Made the first commit, as the answers asked.
init.commit_failed: brain-kit init: the vault is written, but the first commit failed: {detail}
init.no_commit: No commit was made: the first commit is yours. Look at the vault, then commit it with git add -A and git commit.
init.checking: Checking the new vault with brain-kit validate and brain-kit lint --base all:
init.gitignore_header: Written by brain-kit init. Machine-local files, which never belong in the vault's history.
init.gitignore_dependencies: Dependencies: installed per machine, never versioned.
init.gitignore_environment: Local environment files: credentials live here, and must never reach a remote.
init.answer_again: That is not a valid answer for "{answer}"; please answer again.
init.ask_handle: Handle, lowercase letters, digits and dashes, used as human:<handle> [{value}]:
init.ask_repo: GitHub repository as owner/name, or blank for not yet [{value}]:
init.ask_private: The repository must be private: people/ and other personal directories hold data about third parties. Confirm it will be private (y/n) [{value}]:
init.state_unwritable: cannot create the state directory or write machine.json in {state} ({detail}); nothing was written into the vault
init.rolled_back: brain-kit init: {detail}. Everything this run had created was removed, so {dir} is as it was before. Fix the cause and run init again.
init.rollback_incomplete: brain-kit init: {detail}. Removing what this run had created failed for: {left}. Remove those by hand before running init again.
init.commit_skipped: The first commit was not made, because validate or lint found a problem above. Fix it, then commit with git add -A and git commit.
init.nested_repository: Note: this vault is nested inside another git repository, {root}. That repository records the vault as one entry, never its files.
init.unreadable: brain-kit init: {dir} cannot be listed ({detail}), so init cannot be sure nothing in it would be overwritten. Nothing was written.
lang.unsupported_setting: [brain-kit] BRAIN_KIT_LANG={value} is not a supported language ({langs}); using {lang}, from the locale.
init.state_tightened: The state directory {state} already existed with mode {mode}; init set it to 700, because it holds this machine's logs about a private vault.
doctor.only_needs_value: brain-kit doctor: --only needs a comma-separated list of check ids.
doctor.unknown_check: brain-kit doctor: no check is named {ids}. The checks are: {known}.
doctor.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit doctor: "{dir}" is not a directory.
doctor.no_vault: brain-kit doctor: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and {index}).
doctor.heading: brain-kit doctor: {vault}
doctor.check_crashed: this check itself stopped with an error, so it proves nothing: {error}
doctor.node_version.too_old: Node {version} is below the {minimum} this kit needs; install a newer Node.
doctor.node_version.unreadable: cannot read a Node version from "{version}", so it cannot be shown to be recent enough.
doctor.git_present.missing: git did not answer "git --version" (status {status}): it is not on PATH, and nothing in this kit runs without it.
doctor.git_present.unrecognised: "git --version" exited 0 but printed "{output}", which is not a git version: this proves no git is here.
doctor.default_branch_known.unset: origin/HEAD is not set, so the default branch is unknown and every comparison against it is a guess. Run: {command}
doctor.default_branch_known.unrecognised: origin/HEAD reads back as "{output}", which is not a branch of origin. Run: {command}
doctor.default_branch_known.dangling: origin/HEAD points at {branch}, which does not exist. Run: {command}
doctor.hooks_path.not_a_repo: {dir} is not a git repository, so no hook runs on push: a vault with no gate.
doctor.hooks_path.unset: core.hooksPath is not set, so git never runs the vault's gate in {expected}: a clone with no gate. Run: {command}
doctor.hooks_path.unreadable: cannot read core.hooksPath (git exited {status}), so nothing shows the gate runs.
doctor.hooks_path.elsewhere: core.hooksPath is "{value}", not the vault's hook directory {expected}: git runs whatever sits there, not the vault's gate.
doctor.hooks_path.hook_missing: {hook} is missing: core.hooksPath points at a directory with no gate in it.
doctor.hooks_path.hook_empty: {hook} is empty, and a hook with nothing in it refuses nothing.
doctor.hooks_path.hook_not_executable: {hook} is not executable, and git skips a hook it cannot execute: no gate runs.
doctor.config_valid.machine_key: {file} carries a machine-only key at {keys}. Such a key runs something or points at this machine, and belongs in machine.json, never in a file a pull request can change.
doctor.machine_valid.missing: {file} is missing. brain-kit init writes it (brain-kit init --adopt, for a vault that already exists).
doctor.machine_valid.canonical_differs: machine.json records the vault at "{recorded}", but its real path is {actual}.
doctor.state_dir_resolves.use_canonical: reached by this path, the vault's state directory is {used}, which holds no machine.json; the one derived from its real path, {dir}, holds it. Run brain-kit from {path}.
doctor.state_dir_resolves.none: no machine.json in the state directory {dir}, the one every command run from this path looks in.
doctor.state_dir_mode.ok: the state directory {dir} is 0700 and machine.json is 0600
doctor.state_dir_mode.dir_missing: the state directory {dir} does not exist or is not a directory.
doctor.state_dir_mode.dir_mode: the state directory {dir} is {mode}, not {expected}, and it holds logs that quote a private vault.
doctor.state_dir_mode.file_missing: {file} does not exist, so it cannot be 0600.
doctor.kit_version.ok: the configuration and the running engine are both {version}
doctor.kit_version.unknown: cannot read kit_version from {file}, so it cannot be compared with the running engine, {running}.
doctor.kit_version.differs: the configuration was written for kit {configured}, but the engine running is {running}.
doctor.gh_present.missing: gh did not answer "gh --version" (status {status}); propose opens pull requests with it.
doctor.gh_present.unrecognised: "gh --version" exited 0 but printed "{output}", which is not a gh version; propose opens pull requests with it.
doctor.claude_present.unknown: no claude_bin to resolve: {file} is missing or unreadable.
doctor.claude_present.not_found: the configured claude_bin "{bin}" is not an executable file on the machine's path_extra or on PATH.
doctor.claude_present.failed: {bin} resolves but does not run ("--version" exited {status}), which is what a stub left by an interrupted install does.
doctor.claude_present.unrecognised: "{bin} --version" exited 0 but printed "{output}", which is not a version.
doctor.gitignore_node_modules.ok: {pattern} is ignored by {source}, which travels with the vault
doctor.gitignore_node_modules.not_ignore: {pattern} is not ignored. After an npm install in this vault, the secrets rule reads every file the installed kit ships and reports credentials that do not exist, a false refusal. Add it to .gitignore.
doctor.gitignore_node_modules.unknown: cannot ask git whether {pattern} is ignored (status {status}).
doctor.node_version.path_missing: Node {version} runs doctor, but there is no node on PATH, and the gate's hook and brain-kit's own launcher both run the node on PATH: every push is refused.
doctor.node_version.path_failed: the node the gate would run, {bin}, did not answer "--version" (status {status}).
doctor.node_version.path_unrecognised: the node the gate would run, {bin}, printed "{output}" for "--version", which is not a Node version.
doctor.node_version.path_too_old: the node the gate would run, {bin}, is {pathVersion}, below the {minimum} this kit needs.
doctor.node_version.ok_path_differs: Node {version} runs doctor; the gate runs {bin}, Node {pathVersion}
doctor.hooks_path.not_top_level: the vault {dir} is not the top of its git repository ({top}): the hook runs brain-kit from the top level, finds no vault there, and refuses every push.
doctor.hooks_path.differs: {hook} runs on every push, but it differs from the template this kit ships ({template}): if you did not change it on purpose, it may not be the gate.
doctor.brain_kit_on_path.missing: there is no brain-kit on PATH, and the pre-push hook runs the brain-kit on PATH and nothing else: every push is refused. Install brain-kit so it is on the PATH of the shell git runs hooks in.
doctor.brain_kit_on_path.failed: the brain-kit the hook would run, {bin}, did not answer "--version" (status {status}): every push is refused.
doctor.brain_kit_on_path.unrecognised: the brain-kit the hook would run, {bin}, printed "{output}" for "--version", which is not a version: nothing shows it can judge a push.
doctor.brain_kit_on_path.other_version: the hook would run {bin}, version {version}, not the {running} running doctor: pushes are judged by that one.
doctor.config_valid.pattern: {file} has a secret pattern that does not compile: {patterns}. The secrets rule cannot run with it, so lint fails and the gate refuses every push.
doctor.claude_present.machine_invalid: claude_bin is not run: {file} is invalid, and doctor never executes a path from a machine file the kit would refuse.
doctor.claude_present.machine_writable: claude_bin is not run: {file} or its directory can be written by other users, so the path it names may not be yours.
doctor.gitignore_node_modules.local_only: {pattern} is ignored only by {source}, which does not travel with the vault: a second clone or a CI checkout meets the false refusal (the secrets rule reading the installed kit's files and reporting credentials that do not exist). Add it to the vault's .gitignore.
doctor.gitignore_node_modules.tracked: {pattern} is ignored, but {count} file(s) under it are already committed, and ignoring does not untrack them: the secrets rule still reads them. Remove them from the index (git rm -r --cached node_modules).
init.adopt_no_index: brain-kit init --adopt: {dir} has no index.md at its root, so it is not a vault adopt can read. Nothing was written.
init.adopt_commit: brain-kit init --adopt: the answers file {file} says "commit": true, and adopt never commits: the history of an existing vault is yours. Remove it and run again. Nothing was written.
init.adopted: Adopted the vault in {dir}: wrote brain-kit.config.json and .brain-kit/manifest.json ({count} existing files recorded as yours), and changed nothing else in it.
init.adopt_inferred: What adopt read from your notes, each one written into brain-kit.config.json for you to confirm or correct:
init.adopt_checking: The adoption is done: the configuration and the manifest are written. Now brain-kit validate and brain-kit lint --base all check your notes as they were; the exit code that follows is their verdict, not adopt's:
init.adopt_no_commit: No commit was made. If adopt guessed something wrong, or the checks above found something you want to allow, edit brain-kit.config.json: do not run adopt again. Then commit it and .brain-kit/manifest.json yourself.
adopt.note.collection: {dir}/ is a collection of type "{type}" ({count} note(s), all of that type).
adopt.note.domains: these folders mix note types, so they are domains: {dirs}.
adopt.note.extension_enum: "{field}" is a closed list, with the values found per type: {values}. A new value will be reported until it is added here.
adopt.note.extension_kind: "{field}" is declared as {kind}, from every value found.
adopt.note.extension_skipped: "{field}" holds a list or a mapping ({file}, for one), so it was not declared.
adopt.note.confidential_not_boolean: "{field}" marks notes confidential but holds values other than true and false; it is declared boolean, so each of those values will be reported.
adopt.note.confidential_field_unused: no note is marked confidential; "{field}" is declared as the boolean field that would mark one.
adopt.note.confidential_field: privacy.confidential_field is "{field}", the field your notes mark confidentiality with, rather than this language's "{default}".
adopt.note.confidential_dirs: notes are marked confidential in {added}, so the confidential directories are {dirs}. A link into them from outside is now reported.
adopt.note.columns_no_table: {file} has no table, so its column headings stay the defaults.
adopt.note.file_absent: {file} does not exist, so taxonomy.files.{key} is null.
adopt.note.log_absent: no log.md was found; the log stays {file}, which does not exist yet.
adopt.note.log_ambiguous: several log files were found ({files}); the log stays {file}. Set taxonomy.log to the right one.
adopt.note.stale_months: notes in {dir} go stale {months} months after they are written ({count} note(s) agree).
adopt.note.stale_inconsistent: the notes in {dir} do not agree on how long until they go stale, so it has no stale policy.
adopt.note.plain_dates: {count} note(s) write stale_after or generated.at as a plain date, which the format asks to carry a time and a UTC offset; validate.timestamp_deviation is "allow", so each one is a warning rather than a failure.
adopt.note.confidential_links: {count} link(s) from notes outside the confidential directories point into them; lint reports each one as a leak until the link or the marking changes.
adopt.note.extension_reserved: "{field}" is a name the configuration reserves for this machine's own settings, so it was not declared; notes may keep it, and no rule checks it.
init.adopt_unreadable: brain-kit init --adopt: something inside {dir} cannot be read ({detail}), so adopt can neither describe the vault nor record every file of it. Nothing was written.
init.adopt_brain_kit_not_directory: brain-kit init --adopt: {path} exists and is not a directory (a symbolic link or a file). adopt writes the manifest into .brain-kit/ and never through a link; move it away and run again. Nothing was written.
init.adopt_already_vault: brain-kit init --adopt: {dir} is already adopted, so nothing was written. To change what was inferred, edit brain-kit.config.json. To adopt it again from scratch, remove brain-kit.config.json, .brain-kit/manifest.json and {machine}, then run again.
init.adopt_machine_exists: brain-kit init --adopt: {file} already exists, and adopt never overwrites it. If it is left from an earlier adoption of this vault that you are redoing, remove it too and run again. Nothing was written.
adopt.note.collection_reserved: {dir}/ holds notes of type "{type}", but its name is reserved for this machine's settings, so it is not declared as a collection.
adopt.note.enum_type_reserved: "{field}" values for type "{type}" are not listed: that type's name is reserved for this machine's settings, so notes of it are not checked against a list.
adopt.note.extension_unreadable: "{field}" could not be read in {file}; it is declared from the other notes, and validate will point at that one.
adopt.note.confidential_dirs_default: no note is marked confidential outside the default confidential directories, which are kept: {dirs}.
adopt.note.confidential_uncovered: these files are marked confidential where no confidential directory is declared (the vault root, templates, an index or a log); lint will report them: {files}.
adopt.note.stale_inconsistent_default: the notes in {dir} do not agree on how long until they go stale, so its stale policy stays this language's default of {months} months.
adopt.note.stale_default_kept: {dir} goes stale after {months} months, this language's default: no note there carries both stale_after and generated.at.
adopt.note.stale_none: no folder has a stale policy: no notes agree on one, and no folder has this language's default.
update.usage:
Usage: brain-kit update [dir] [--check]
       brain-kit update [dir] --accept <path>

Refreshes the files the kit manages in the vault found from dir (default: the current directory), by checksum, as .brain-kit/manifest.json records them. A managed file you have not edited is replaced with this kit's version. A managed file you edited is never overwritten: when this kit has a newer version, it is written beside it as <name>.brain-kit-new for you to take what you want from. A seeded note is yours and is never touched. A managed file you deleted is reported and not recreated. Line endings are kept as each file has them. After a run with no failed write, the configuration's kit_version is set to this kit's version.

  --check          write nothing; exit 1 when anything would change or needs you, 0 otherwise
  --accept <path>  you have dealt with this kit's version of a managed file (path relative to the vault): remember it, so it is not offered again until the kit changes it, and remove its .brain-kit-new; your file is not touched. For a managed file you deleted on purpose, stop tracking it.

It refuses, writing nothing, when the manifest cannot be read, when this kit is older than the configuration's kit_version, and when the configuration's lang is not the language the managed files were written in.

Exit codes: 0 everything current, 1 failure or (with --check) something pending, 2 usage or not inside a vault, 3 done but something needs you.
update.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit update: "{dir}" is not a directory.
update.no_vault: brain-kit update: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and index.md).
update.manifest_unreadable:
brain-kit update: {detail}
Nothing was written. Without a readable manifest update cannot tell the kit's files from yours, so it refuses rather than treat the vault as having nothing to update. If the vault has a commit that holds it, git checkout -- .brain-kit/manifest.json brings it back.
update.would_refresh: Would update {file} to this kit's version.
update.offered: {file} was edited, so it was left as it is. This kit's version was written beside it as {new}. Take what you want from it into your file, then run: {command}
update.would_offer: {file} was edited, so it would be left as it is, and this kit's version would be written beside it as {new}.
update.offer_blocked: {file} was edited and this kit has a newer version of it, but {new} is already there, so nothing was written. Take what you want from it into your file, then run: {command}
update.missing: {file} is managed by the kit but no longer exists; it was not recreated. If you removed it on purpose, run: {command}
update.not_regular: {file} is not a regular file inside the vault (it is a link, a directory, or reached through a linked directory), so it was left alone.
update.unreadable: {file} could not be read ({detail}), so it was left alone.
update.kept: {file} was edited; this kit has nothing newer for it, so it was left as it is.
update.not_in_kit: {file} is managed, but this kit no longer ships it; it was left as it is.
update.raced: {file} changed while update was running, so it was left as it is. Run brain-kit update again.
update.manifest_write_failed: brain-kit update: .brain-kit/manifest.json could not be rewritten ({detail}), so the hashes of any file updated above are the old ones: those files read as current, but a later kit version will be offered beside them instead of replacing them.
update.summary: {managed} managed file(s): {refreshed} updated, {current} already current, {kept} edited and kept, {attention} needing you; {seeded} seeded note(s) left alone.
update.check_pending: {count} file(s) pending: run brain-kit update to apply what it can, and see above for what needs you.
update.accept_with_check: brain-kit update: --accept writes the manifest, and --check writes nothing; use one or the other.
update.check_summary: {managed} managed file(s): {refreshed} would be updated, {current} already current, {kept} edited and kept, {attention} needing you; {seeded} seeded note(s) left alone.
update.kit_older: brain-kit update: this kit is {running}, older than the {configured} this vault's configuration was written for, so it would put back older versions of the kit's files. Nothing was written. Update brain-kit, then run this again.
update.lang_changed: brain-kit update: the kit's files in this vault were written in {recorded}, and the configuration now says lang is {configured}. Their language is fixed when the vault is made: refreshing them from the other language would replace every contract file with one whose links point at folders this vault does not have. Nothing was written. Set lang back to update them.
update.manifest_not_regular: brain-kit update: {file} is not a regular file (a link, or something else), so update will not write it. Nothing was written.
update.manifest_outside: brain-kit update: {file} is reached through a link that leads outside the vault, so update will not write it. Nothing was written.
update.manifest_not_writable: brain-kit update: {dir} is not writable, so the manifest could not be updated after the files were. Nothing was written.
update.config_not_editable: brain-kit update: this kit is newer than the kit_version in {file}, but that file is not a regular file holding exactly one kit_version update can set. Nothing was written.
update.bumped: Set kit_version in the configuration from {from} to {to}.
update.would_bump: Would set kit_version in the configuration from {from} to {to}.
update.accept_outside: brain-kit update: "{path}" is not a file inside the vault.
update.accept_not_managed: brain-kit update: {file} is not a file the kit manages, so there is nothing to accept.
update.accept_not_executable: brain-kit update: {file} is not executable, and git skips a hook it cannot execute, so accepting it would leave the vault with no gate. Nothing was written. Run {command}, then accept it again.
update.accept_recorded: Recorded this kit's version of {file}: it will not be offered again until the kit changes it. Your file was not touched.
update.accept_dropped: {file} is no longer tracked by update.
update.accept_new_left: {new} is a directory, so it was left where it is.
update.accept_nothing: {file} has nothing to accept: the manifest already records this kit's version of it, and there is nothing beside it.
update.accept_last_entry: brain-kit update: {file} is the last file the manifest lists, and a manifest cannot be empty. Nothing was written.
init.gitignore_update: Written by brain-kit update: versions offered beside a file you edited, and temporary files a stopped run can leave.
